title: Reach channel registry (src/config/reach-channels.yml)
$comment: road-to-internet-reach Phase 1. Validated by src/scripts/check_reach_channels.ts (task check-reach-channels). SCOPE: standalone operator tooling — the registry answers 'which external backend does a reach recipe need, is it healthy, is its install command pinned'. The Phase 0 benchmark returned band: stop, so no channel here is routed, recommended, or agent-facing; nothing in this schema may be read as a routing table. Lifecycle vocabulary is REUSED from docs/contracts/provider-lifecycle.md — never fork a second enum. NO $ref / patternProperties / if-then anywhere: the validator is the Draft-07 subset exported by src/scripts/validate_frontmatter.ts (type, required, properties, additionalProperties:false, items, minItems, pattern, minLength, enum), so the install-string schema is inlined per platform key on purpose.

schema_version.description: Registry format version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change.

channels.description: Channel list. A channel is a retrieval need (repository metadata, a feed, a page read); its `backends` are the ORDERED candidate tools that can satisfy it — first healthy candidate wins, so switching a backend is reordering this list, never editing code. Order carries meaning; channel order does not.

id.description: Channel slug — unique within the registry, lowercase.

description.description: What the channel retrieves, in operator terms. Never a recommendation to use it.

tier.description: Access cost to the operator: `zero-config` = no credential; `free-key` = a free token/API key the operator provisions; `login` = an authenticated account session. Documents setup effort only — it does not authorize credential harvesting of any kind.

lifecycle.description: Reused verbatim from docs/contracts/provider-lifecycle.md § tiers. `experimental` = shape is right, no maintainer-verified real run; `stable` = maintainer-verified against a real run at least once; `deprecated` = successor declared, kept for one migration window (see removal_after / replacement); `community` = externally contributed, best-effort.

override_key.description: Settings key by which an operator pins one backend for this channel, bypassing candidate order.

last_verified.description: ISO date the channel's backends and pins were last checked by a human. MUST be quoted in YAML — an unquoted date parses as a timestamp, not a string, and fails this type check loudly. Replaces a scheduled network CI job: staleness is checked offline against this field.

removal_after.description: Deprecation path, optional. Only meaningful with lifecycle `deprecated`: until this date the channel still probes with a warning; past it the doctor reports the channel as removed and the staleness lint flags its continued presence in this file.

replacement.description: Deprecation path, optional. Channel id that supersedes this one.

credential_path.description: Optional path to the credential file this channel's backend reads (`~` is expanded). The doctor ONLY stats it, to warn when it is group- or world-readable — it never opens it, never hashes it, and never reports its contents. Declared here because reach_doctor.ts enforces this schema at runtime and additionalProperties is false, so a field the code supports must be declared or no registry could use it. No shipped channel declares one.

backends.description: Ordered candidate tools. Each is an alternative that satisfies the channel on its own — not a pipeline stage.

id.description: Backend slug — unique within its channel.

probe_cmd.description: Bare executable name resolved on PATH. No path separators, no shell — the probe layer spawns it directly through hardenedSpawnEnv(). MUST equal this backend's `id`: a backend probes its own binary and nothing else, so a report row labelled `gh` can never be the health of `/bin/sh`. The equality is a cross-field rule this Draft-07 subset cannot express, so it is asserted by check_probe_cmd_binding() in src/scripts/check_reach_channels.ts and reported as rule `probe_cmd-binding`.

probe_args.description: Side-effect-free probe arguments only — a version / help / status query. The item pattern is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist: an argument must be flag-shaped (`--version`, `-V`, `version`, `rate_limit`) and nothing else. A denylist was tried first and leaked — it admitted `cp`, `cat`, `-c`, `--data-binary` and every URL, so `probe_cmd: sh` + `probe_args: ["-c", "<payload>"]` passed the gate. What is actually true after the allowlist plus the probe_cmd===id binding plus runtime enforcement of this schema in reach_doctor.collect(): no path, no URL, no shell metacharacter, and no `-c`-style inline payload can reach the spawned child, and the child is the backend's own binary. This bounds the argument shape; it is not a proof that every upstream binary is side-effect-free under every flag — that judgement stays with the human who adds the backend.

install.description: Human-performed install prescription per platform, selected by process.platform with `default` as the fallback. The package NEVER runs these: prescription-first, no auto-install, no piped remote installer. Platform keys are optional; `default` is not.

default.description: PINNING CONTRACT — an install prescription is EITHER (a) a command carrying an explicit version specifier (`name==1.2.3`, `name@22`, `--version 2.96.0`, or a whitespace-separated exact `1.2.3` triple), OR (b) an `os-baseline: <explanation>` sentinel for a tool the platform ships and no package install is prescribed for. Everything else FAILS: an unpinned command, and any moving-target source — `latest`, `main`, `master`, `HEAD`, `archive/…`, `.zip`, `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.xz`. This mechanizes the supply-chain intake floor (verify, pin, lock, never pipe a remote script to a shell) instead of asserting it.
